# Execution owner — September12

Parent67e314e. Reference6f87158d77f66a36d5f8bbe915170b24e2acabe8,
Tinygrad0.14.0. Reviewed engine/realize.py in full and its ProgramInfo,
GraphRunner, CUDA graph and cu_time_execution consumers. C execution owner is
src/engine/schedule.c; CUDA events/resources remain in src/runtime_cuda.c.
This is a source review and supported-path repair, not full-owner equivalence.

## Observed repairs and correspondence

| Pinned expression / branch | Probe result | C owner / expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ProgramInfo.launch_dims | Preserves0,-1,2**31,8.5,inf,nan; never substitutes1 | poly_launch_arg_to_i64 and poly_resolve_runner_launch_dims reject invalid values at the bounded C integer launch boundary, before conversion/execution. Candidate dimensions publish together. |
| ProgramInfo unit dimensions | Default global size1,1,1 | poly_runner_apply_program_launch_info always copies metadata, including unit dimensions; interpreter runners otherwise remain zeroed. |
| get_call_outs_ins PROGRAM/COPY/encdec/other/SINK | Metadata; out0/in1; out0/rest; empty; empty | poly_call_get_outs_ins implements that classification. SINK dependency walking remains private to ProgramInfo construction. |
| exec_kernel(wait=True), track_stats | Instrumented runtime receives wait and returns elapsed; update_stats=False suppresses counters | poly_exec_linear_program forwards wait independently of accounting; CUDA returns event time, synchronous C backends use call wall time. |
| exec_graph -> CUDAGraph.__call__ -> cu_time_execution | Same waited runtime contract as kernel execution; source inspection | poly_exec_linear_graph uses shared CUDA event timing. Actual PG CUDA ordinary/graph tests require positive accounted elapsed and correct output. |
| run_linear wait or DEBUG>=2 | Pinned dispatch policy | poly_run_linear applies the same condition before dispatch. No extra CUDA synchronization after a waited end event. |

poly_linear_lane_vars implements the variable-map merge in unwrap_multi/exec_kernel.
The analyzer exposed a real count overflow: INT_MAX+1, observed under UBSan in
count-red.log. Count and byte capacity now reject before copying caller inputs;
the permanent regression also checks ordinary duplicate-key replacement. The
POLY_TESTING wrapper exposes this private admission boundary without changing
the production ABI. The initial regression build lacked limits.h and failed
compilation; that build is not behavioral evidence.

CUDA event setup/cleanup is one C-only ownership implementation of
cu_time_execution, shared by ordinary and graph launch. No public ABI/layout
change, graph dialect or additional scheduler. Package versions stay unchanged.

red-batch.log contains five genuine failed checks: launch admission, access
classification, INTERP timing, CUDA timing and CUDA graph timing. Its sixth
failure used an incorrect nested-compilation expectation and is NOT defect
evidence. green.log then exposed the unit-dimension initialization interaction
introduced by strict admission; green-final.log verifies its correction.

## Two rejected hypotheses

- GraphRunner allocates all captured CALL arguments, not just ProgramInfo.globals.
  The instrumented pin probe observes both buffers allocated. PG behavior stays.
- lower_and_compile collects/compiles nested CALLs as a cache side effect, but
  final substitution does not enter an opaque graph CALL. The pin probe observes
  the original inner LINEAR/SINK unchanged. The corrected permanent C test
  preserves this boundary; no recursive-substitution patch was made. PG's
  synchronous compiler does not reproduce the nested cache side effect.

## Remaining contracts by upstream owner

All25 formerly generic pending execution rows were reviewed. Their specific
dispositions live in scheduler_codegen.json; aggregate rows overlap children.
Neither a pending diagnostic nor an unimplemented capability is an approval.

- get_call_outs_ins: all pinned branches implemented and exercised. Close only
  this row with source-bound execution. Re-run existing _resolve and
  get_call_arg_uops controls without changing their established semantics.
- exec_kernel/exec_graph: supported ordinary/CUDA-graph timing repaired. Full
  rows still inherit runtime scalar-domain, timeout, multi-device and backend
  graph-scope differences. C get_runtime uses context-owned runner resources;
  it does not load TinyELF. Existing PG-DIV-004 documents binary reconstruction.
- get_runtime: exact CALL-device cache keys are covered by the previous batch.
  PG_PCACHE=0 disables both lookup and insertion; upstream cache=False can read
  an existing runtime but suppresses insertion. Do not call these identical.
- optimize_local_size: missing standalone postcompile tuner. Upstream reuses
  one uncached runtime, tests valid candidate workgroups twice, and rewrites
  PROGRAM dimensions. PG's compiler-selected workgroups/BEAM are not this pass.
  This is concrete implementation work, not source-evidence housekeeping.
- compile_linear/lower_and_compile/_compile_kernel/_get_call_to_compile:
  supported SINK/partial-PROGRAM resume and BEAM propagation have existing
  controls. Remaining contracts: local-size pass, worker Context transport,
  nested compile-cache side effect, HCQ wrapper admission and validation.
- time_call: C returns a bounded repeated minimum with early stop/grid scaling;
  upstream yields an iterator with cache policy, clear_l2 and timeout. Existing
  C BEAM adapter/deadline controls do not prove whole-function equivalence.
- estimate_uop/track_stats/get_call_kernels/get_call_name: PROGRAM/COPY and
  CUDA-graph counters exist; PROFILE events, display identities, HCQ estimates
  and encdec estimates are not complete. Waited timing was a real defect, not
  a reason to certify all diagnostic/statistics branches.
- exec_copy: existing allocator copies and empty-copy controls remain. The
  pinned DISK optimized copy and multi-device transfer branches require their
  own scoped evidence. No copying behavior changed in this batch.
- exec_encdec: NV hardware allocator encode/decode, not HF/GGUF file decoding.
  No backend implementation in PG; the repaired access helper does not enable it.
- _validate/exec_validate: CPU shadow-buffer validation is not implemented.
- exec_hcq/link_linear/get_call_var_uops: HCQ lowering/linking/address-table
  construction is not implemented. get_call_var_uops is used by CPU HCQ command
  generation, not ordinary exec_kernel; do not add an unused wrapper.
- unwrap_multi: existing same-device structural lanes differ from upstream zip
  admission; genuine accelerator multi-device support remains separately scoped.
- pm_exec/run_linear/@file: aggregate pending follows the concrete missing
  contracts above. No ordinary execution fallback was added.

## Next connected work

Resolve the supported local-size selection and its launch-domain/cache contract
as one owner batch, with real CUDA and WebGPU measurements. Keep optional HCQ,
NV codec, CPU validation and profiling decisions visible and separate. Do not
call the wave closed, nor demand an entire compiler reread from this repair.

## Analyzer interpretation

Initial scan:3 schedule.c reports,0 runtime_cuda.c reports. The binding-count
report was not an immutable-count false positive: signed addition could overflow
at INT_MAX with a device binding. Earlier broad descriptions of this trace as a
count contradiction were insufficient; the observed UBSan failure settles it.

The other two traces assume zero CALL buffer arguments with nonzero
ProgramInfo.globals, then dereference unresolved storage. Both ordinary and
graph dispatch first call poly_call_get_outs_ins -> poly_call_apply_program_info,
which rejects every global outside [0,n_args). The analyzer assumes that helper
returned success while discarding its bound relationship. No suppressions or
redundant downstream guards were added. Final counts belong in results.md;
these dispositions do not claim a project-wide analyzer-clean result.

| uop_print_one/poly_uop_str | uop/ops.py:UOp.argstr/__repr__, delegated to pretty_print. C-only checked size measurement and exact allocation replace the unsafe fixed 256-byte buffer. A 600-digit endpoint repro gives an ASan write into a freed allocation before the fix. Existing text representation is preserved; full Python repr spelling is not claimed. |
| poly_resolve_linear_param | engine/realize.py:_resolve: PARAM slot, recursive MSTACK, direct PARAM base in SHRINK/MSELECT, otherwise identity. Metadata-preserving reconstruction; C adds invalid-slot/allocation checks. Permanent structural controls cover every branch. |

Construction rejects unordered/nonnumeric/reversed intervals at the C API.
No runtime fallback, new placement input, multi-GPU support or public binding
domain expansion is introduced. NaN literal arithmetic remains separate from
ordered interval reasoning. Generated mirrors are regenerated, not hand-edited.

Red evidence: red-runtime.log, red-python-bounds-corrected.log,
typed-core-red.log (multiple_of; early test assertion leaves owners unreleased),
typed-full-fold-red.log (incorrect MAX), paired with probe.py/typed-tinygrad.log.
Correction: typed-fold-red.log and typed-fold-suite-red.log used symbolic_simple,
which does not contain the full matcher's point/MAX rules. Their unchanged PARAM
is not valid evidence of a missing point rule. The permanent regression now uses
poly_symbolic, matching Tinygrad's simplify(). Float LOAD reduction remains a
passing control, not an invented defect.

Build corrections: strict Wasm diagnosed strdup declarations and the missing
bigint.h include in engine/schedule.c. The first broad syntax sweep included
native-only CUDA/POSIX tests; its errors do not describe the maintained Wasm
target. typed-wasm-owned-syntax.log checks the actual affected Wasm owners.

## Analyzer disposition

The five-owner scan reports eight warnings, not a clean analyzer gate. The two
new IR warnings stop immediately after br_param_bound publishes allocated limbs
into a PolyArg; neither trace identifies an exit that bypasses cleanup_node_arg.
All subsequent failure branches target that cleanup, and normal construction
copies into UOp storage before the same cleanup frees both endpoint payloads.
Both endpoints are BIGINT in the codec regression, including every truncation,
with leak detection enabled. No warning suppression or ownership workaround.
The remaining symbolic and engine warnings are the previously reviewed
opcode/immutable-count/global-admission contradictions; their line numbers moved.
Raw current traces: typed-analyzer.log and typed-ir-analyzer-trace.log.

## ABI consumer and proof limitations

The optional Z3 harness initially segfaulted because its raw ctypes mirrors still
used an obsolete DType, undersized argument union, int64 PARAM endpoints and old
enum values. Updated actual C layouts and added an ABI79 guard plus deterministic
typed-endpoint/RANGE controls. GDB and ctypes agree: DType24, PolyArg104,
PolyParamArg304, UOp312 bytes. General64 and division64 proofs pass. Fixed-width
mode still fails uint8_add_wrap_cmp: (x+10)<5 with x in[250,251] simplifies to
False, but modular x=250 gives True. The pinned Tinygrad probe has the same
result. No core workaround, suppression or green claim for that stricter oracle.

Reusing the existing argument representation increases PolyParamArg from112 to
304 bytes (+192 per allocated metadata record), measured in typed-param-layout.log.
This is host graph metadata, not device residency or an HLB attribution result.
Runtime int32 binding admission remains PG-PARITY-028. General arbitrary-width
derived min/max optimization is not claimed by the endpoint representation fix.

# Supported compiler/runtime owner review — September12

Pin: Tinygrad v0.14.0/6f87158d77f66a36d5f8bbe915170b24e2acabe8.
This is a bounded source review, not closure of scheduler_codegen.

## Completed blocks

- `codegen/simplify.py:mark_range_mod` -> `src/codegen/simplify.c:mark_range_mod`:
  first eligible match, WARP/DEVICE exclusion, constant extent and exact
  divisibility. The C PolyInt division implements Python integer arithmetic;
  absent rewrite context or failed allocation declines the optional rewrite.
  Nine configuration/first-match controls match the pinned probe. No fix needed.
- `engine/realize.py:get_call_arg_uops` -> `poly_call_n_buffer_args` and
  `poly_call_buffer_arg`: remove only bound variables from CALL operands,
  preserving order, duplicates and unbound variables. C invalid-call/index
  checks are API admission mechanics. Paired probe and permanent control pass.
- `UOp._min_max` wide-operand boundary: observed uint64 LOAD SHR62/FLOORDIV2**62
  bounds [0,1] instead of [0,3]. Reuse the existing exact integer query before
  int64 projection. The AND3 control already returned [0,3]. No new interval
  engine, graph dialect, metadata layout or binding ABI.
- Exact interval array ownership: allocation failure previously dereferenced
  NULL during cleanup. The red-first failure-injection test covers rejection
  and a subsequent usable query. Cleanup now checks the candidate array.
- Reduction consumer: the upper clamp already survived this interval defect.
  Exact graph assertion and four substitutions now preserve that control.
  Do not claim an observed reduction wrong result was repaired.

## Connected owners inspected, with limits

- Read all pinned codegen/simplify.py and the corresponding range merging,
  substitution, modulo splitting and reduction drivers. Existing dimension,
  axes, guard and failed-publication regressions remain controls. Optional
  substitution failure declining a rewrite is not equivalent to publishing
  failed JIT lowering. Remaining metadata domain prevents whole-file closure.
- Read pinned schedule/memory.py against memory.c: held/device admission,
  BUFFER/MSELECT/MSTACK collection, live intervals, separate copy lanes,
  extended copy holds, 256-byte alignment, close-before-open events, arena
  offsets and SHRINK/BITCAST replacement. Existing huge-size/retry/tuple-view
  controls cover the supported C mechanics; this is not a proof of every
  arithmetic path or multi-device hardware support. Historical rows are not
  wholesale rebound to current tests.
- Read realization preparation/execution and CUDA GraphRunner preparation.
  CUDA graphs intentionally allocate all resolved CALL operands, matching
  GraphRunner.__init__; ordinary exec_kernel only allocates PROGRAM globals.
  Do not change the former to match the latter.
- `_resolve` maps PARAM slots, recursively resolves MSTACK, and replaces a
  direct PARAM base of SHRINK/MSELECT, preserving metadata. C adds bounds and
  allocation checks. Existing tuple-view tests are not a direct control of
  every resolver branch, so its pending row is retained.
- PROGRAM dispatch differs syntactically: Polygrad uses ProgramInfo.target,
  while exec_kernel chooses devices from the CALL. Normal constructed graphs
  agree. Cross-target/adversarial admissibility needs a direct probe; no
  unsupported-input equivalence or defect claim is made here.

## Analyzer disposition

Five owners, eight reports, exit2; raw traces in analyzer.log. These are
infeasible under the following reviewed invariants, not suppressed warnings:

- symbolic.c:4625/4629: try_nest_by_factor's sole caller admits only FLOORDIV
  or FLOORMOD. The trace assumes neither. FLOORMOD allocates b_parts and checks
  failure; FLOORDIV never enters the b_parts branch.
- symbolic.c:5334/5336: immutable child source counts determine both capacity
  and copies. Zero capacity cannot be followed by a positive copy count.
- simplify.c:1027: same unchanged edge-capacity/count contradiction reviewed
  in compiler-tail-20260911.6j2tqN/source-reviewed.md.
- jit.c:655 and engine/schedule.c:3573/3948: unchanged source; edge count,
  scalar-variable count/fill predicate, and PROGRAM globals admission
  contradictions documented in scalar-domains-20260912.mqPW1k/source-reviewed.md.
- schedule/memory.c emits no report. No project-wide analyzer-clean claim.

## Remaining obligations

Temporary PARAM endpoints are int64: fractional/infinite/full-uint64 metadata
still has no complete correspondence. This fix repairs derived representable
bounds, not the metadata domain or the separate int32 runtime binding limit.
Whole-owner publication requires direct resolver/target-dispatch controls and
remaining supported symbolic/specification correspondence. Worker/assembly
diagnostics, forced dtype emulation, image/DSP, device-axis/global_prod_max and
HCQ/validation routes need their existing explicit capability dispositions;
pending review does not make a route optional. No ABI widening or fallback.

# Compiler domain owner dispositions

Reference: Tinygrad v0.14.0/6f87158d77f6. Current owner review covers complete
gpudims.py and simplify.py, with source/probe correspondence in correspondence.md.
This is not full scheduler_codegen closure or a release certificate.

## Blocks with completed correspondence

- `_split_dims`: identity for in-cap dimensions; three-axis padding, inclusive
  square-root divisor search, ordered spill/wrap, prime failure and trailing
  unit removal match the reference. C launch caps are three integer axes;
  checked int64 multiplication is the existing backend dimension boundary.
  Symbolic cap predicates must be decidable. A split factors an integer, never
  a variable's maximum. Dimension expressions are simplified at add_gpudims,
  matching ssimplify before get_grouped_dims.
- `get_grouped_dims`: reverse before legalization and reverse returned indices;
  group first, split only after grouping fails with at most three axes;
  uncapped list, SPECIAL names, flattened stride sum and logical-axis
  reconstruction all use existing UOp arithmetic/symbolic owners. Scratch
  capacity is max(rank,3), not a fixed-rank graph representation. Existing
  grouped-axis, repeated merge, uncapped-rank and oversized-launch tests pass.
- `flatten_range`: partition trailing operands by bool/void dtype, preserve
  ordered backedges and leading values, derive ordinary active ranges through
  the shared range query, and preserve node metadata on replacement. Its
  scratch failure declines rewriting. Fatal range-cache allocation policy is
  unchanged. Existing backedge and END-expression normalization tests pass.
- `mark_gated`: coordinate/valid extraction; left-to-right AND traversal;
  last guard per range, maximum across INDEX uses, and full original bound
  for any ungated use follow the reference. Private pass-state failure marker
  prevents an incomplete inspection from publishing a smaller range. The
  marker is cleared at the same SINK dictionary boundary; no public API or
  new lifetime owner. Existing max-guard and new failed-scan/recovery tests pass.
- `pm_load_collapse`: first rule requires (ADD,0), exactly one trailing range;
  second requires weakint x, commutative ADD and proven no_load predicates.
  Its called reduce_load_collapse/temporary-parameter algorithm remains a
  separately pending dependency. Completing matcher admission does not certify
  all possible temporary bounds. Negative axes/arity and overflow controls pass.

## Repairs inside still-pending aggregate blocks

- `pm_reduce_collapse` and `pm_reduce_simplify`: complete ADD metadata admission,
  boolean zero matching and allow_any_len admission were repaired. Duplicate
  zero tests consolidated; reduce_unparented deliberately keeps its broader
  operator/axes contract. The composed symbolic matcher and temporary bound
  dependency prevent a whole-aggregate equivalence claim.
- `add_gpudims`: source dimensions now use ssimplify-equivalent symbolic
  normalization. Existing C-only has_threads admission and absent renderer
  global_prod_max/device-axis lowering need separate capability disposition.
  CUDA/WebGPU reference renderers inherit global_prod_max=None. No unsupported
  backend capability was enabled or silently approved.

## Remaining named obligations (not new bugs)

- Temporary PARAM bounds: Tinygrad uses PyConst endpoints, C ParamArg and the
  legacy cache use int64. Executed fractional/unbounded reference controls and
  the unbounded PG regression do not show a wrong result. Exact fractional,
  infinite and unsigned64 metadata correspondence is still unproved. Carry
  this into the symbolic/metadata owner batch, not another speculative rewrite.
- Range merging/mod splitting were read end to end. Existing failure behavior
  and tests remain useful; wider bigint/metadata dependency certification is
  still pending. No opportunistic source rewrite was made without a red case.
- PROGRAM worker/assembly diagnostics, image-specific gater, global_prod_max,
  DEVICE-axis, DSP and forced dtype emulation retain explicit scope questions.
  Pure aggregate @file rows cannot close while their dependencies remain open.

## Analyzer

The same included-edge sum determines allocation capacity and the later fill
loop. The remaining trace assumes capacity==0, then executes a positive-edge
loop, an infeasible combination for immutable source nodes. The two-file run
still exits2; no project-wide analyzer-clean claim or warning suppression.
